# Cycle log

One entry per cycle, newest last. What settled, what was opened and why, what
was refused, and anything the chain did that `CHAIN.md` does not say. Written
by the agent at the end of every cycle, per `CYCLE.md` step 8.

## Cycle 1 - 2026-09-09 00:13 UTC - full (hand-run by the operator)

The first cycle. Run by hand against live chain state to prove the procedure
in `CYCLE.md` works end to end before `loop.sh` runs it unattended.

**Settled:** nothing. The ledger was empty.

**Cost of a move**, at block 58,107,259, gas 0.2305 gwei, ETH 2,491.40 USDG:
Morpho round trip 0.1618 USDG (6.5 bps at full size), ERC-4626 vault 0.5129
(20.5 bps), Uniswap v3 LP 0.5451 (21.8 bps), idle zero. Well under the 25 bps
that would have made this an idle cycle.

**Quoted:** 20 venues above the 25,000 USDG depth floor, plus two more
(below). After `strategy/venue-filters.json`, nine carried a rate worth
using. The board is thinner than its 329 rows suggest.

**Opened:**

- `a00001` Morpho `0xaa586d26`, 250 USDG, 3 days, forecasting 45% gross and
  **+24.03 bps** net against 81.14% advertised. The rate was 63.46%
  yesterday, 78.02% five minutes before the quote, and 81.14% at entry, all
  at 99.95% utilization - an adaptive IRM climbing because demand exceeds
  supply. Its own two-week history read 10.32% and 43.51% in the only two
  windows it traded. Forecasting above that range and far below spot.
- `a00002` Morpho `0xaba3ac50`, 250 USDG, 7 days, forecasting 9.5% gross and
  **+10.99 bps** net against 9.78% advertised. Utilization is 99.99999% - 33
  raw units of free liquidity on a 46,836 USDG market. The low-margin arm,
  opened deliberately.
- `a00003` idle, 500 USDG, 3 days, **0 bps**. The measured baseline.

That is the whole bankroll: 1,000 of 1,000 USDG committed.

**Refused or skipped:**

- The deepest Morpho markets (313M at 4.67%, 96M at 3.83%, 31M at 5.03%)
  forecast under 2 bps net over seven days, below the operator's 5 bps floor.
  The safest venues on the chain are the ones the caps will not let us touch.
- Every ERC-4626 vault with a trustworthy rate pays under 4.8%, against the
  11.3% a vault round trip needs over seven days. The 20.5 bps round trip is
  what rules them out, not the rates.
- Every Uniswap v3 pool. Live rates read 42-45% APY, but each is measured
  over a 404-second window, under the 3,600-second minimum in
  `strategy/venue-filters.json`. On the evidence in `core/tests/test_settle.py`
  an LP position here is a bet on ETH being flat, not on fee income: a 0.054%
  ETH move cost 0.0675 USDG on a 250 USDG position while the whole share of
  fee growth over the same window earned 0.000028.
- Vault `0xe24cabdf`, advertising 2021% on 612,295 USDG. Over the
  `max_plausible_apy` ceiling. Not banned, but it needs a second reading in a
  later cycle before it can be allocated to.
- Two vaults advertising -240% and -321%. A negative rate is a loss on entry.

**Strategy changed:** `strategy/risk.json` `max_venue_share` 0.25 to 0.5, and
a new agent-owned `max_market_share_usdg` of 250. The seed comment claimed
0.25 meant one open position per market. It does not: `core/ledger.py` groups
the cap by the venue address, and all 186 USDG Morpho markets share one
Morpho Blue contract, so 0.25 meant one Morpho market ever. The engine's venue
axis is contract risk, which half the bankroll is the right cap for; market
concentration is a separate axis the engine cannot see, so the agent holds it.
Changed before anything was opened.

**For the operator** (also in `journal/proposals.md`):

- Both allocatable markets sit at 99.95% and 99.99999% utilization. That is
  not a coincidence - Morpho's supply rate is the borrow rate times
  utilization, so the highest-paying market is always the one with the least
  exit liquidity. At 100% utilization a withdraw reverts, and nothing in the
  engine refuses a market on that ground. Paper settlement reads the share
  price and will happily realize a return the position could not actually
  have exited.
- The cycle quoted 22 venues against its own budget of 20. `--top` selects
  the deepest recorded rows, and depth on this chain is inversely related to
  rate, so the depth-ranked top 20 missed both rate-carrying candidates in the
  25,000-500,000 USDG band. Ranking by recorded rate above the depth floor
  would have found them inside the budget.

**Chain notes for `CHAIN.md`:** Morpho market `0xaa586d26` moved 63.46% to
81.14% in about 25 hours and 78.02% to 81.14% in five minutes, both at pinned
utilization. A Morpho rate on 4663 is not a slowly moving number and a quote
more than a few minutes old is not a quote.

**RPC:** 6 requests / 19 calls for the cost table, 46 / 233 for the board
quote, then a handful per allocation. The whole cycle cost under 80 HTTP
requests. See `journal/rpc-usage.jsonl`.

**Added after the allocations, not before:** `min_free_liquidity_multiple` of
4.0 in `strategy/venue-filters.json`. Both of this cycle's positions were
opened before the exit-liquidity problem was understood, and both would fail
the new rule. They stay open - `min_hold_minutes` forbids closing them and
closing a position to tidy the record is the one thing this repo must not do.
Cycle 2 will most likely allocate nothing under this rule, and that is the
honest consequence of what cycle 1 found rather than a reason to weaken it.

## Cycle 6 - 2026-09-10 01:14 UTC - full

**Settled:** nothing due. `a00003` (idle, 500 USDG, 3 d) still has about 1.96
days left. Nothing to score, no retro, no strategy edit - nothing settled to
justify one.

**Cost of a move**, block 58,999,931, gas 0.162 gwei: Morpho round trip 4.6
bps at 250 USDG, ERC-4626 vault 14.6 bps, Uniswap v3 LP 15.8 bps. Well under
`max_round_trip_bps` (25).

**Quoted:** first attempt hit the public RPC's throttling after nine retries
on the vault log scan and raised `RpcError`; a straight retry a minute later
completed clean. 20 rows above the 25,000 USDG depth floor. After
`strategy/venue-filters.json` (kind, positive rate, rate window, free
liquidity): 5 Morpho markets and 4 ERC-4626 vaults had a usable rate; every
Uniswap v3 pool's rate window was 403 seconds, still under the 3,600s floor,
so none were quotable in principle.

**Opened:**

- `a00004` Morpho `0xaa586d26` (the same market voided as `a00001` in cycle
  1), 250 USDG, 7 days, forecasting 15.25% gross and **+22.7 bps** net
  against 17.95% advertised. Utilization fell from 99.95% at cycle 1's void
  to 90.3% now and the rate from 81.1% to 17.9% - free liquidity is 33,856
  USDG, 135x this size, clearing `min_free_liquidity_multiple` (4.0) by a
  wide margin where cycle 1 failed it. Seven days, not three: even the
  advertised rate passed straight through nets only 9.1 bps at three days,
  under this strategy's own 10 bps floor, and 15.25% haircut-adjusted nets
  only 7.2 bps at three days. Seven days is the shortest horizon this
  market's economics clear. Known risk, taken deliberately: this market's own
  two-week history spans 10.3-81.1%, so the bet is that the drop to 90.3%
  utilization is mean reversion from cycle 1's spike, not a new plateau - and
  the position cannot be exited before the forecast horizon regardless of
  what the rate does in between.
- `a00005` idle, 250 USDG, 7 days, **0 bps**, the rest of the capital freed by
  voiding `a00001`/`a00002`. Matched to `a00004`'s horizon so `idle_delta` has
  a baseline for the same window.

That is the full bankroll: 1,000 of 1,000 USDG committed (500 in `a00003`,
250 in `a00004`, 250 in `a00005`).

**Refused or skipped:**

- All four deep Morpho markets (313.9M at 4.07%, 96.9M at 3.64%, 31.2M at
  5.03%, 27.2M at 2.43% advertised) fail their 7-day hurdle after the 0.85
  haircut: 1.9, 1.3, 3.5, and -0.6 net bps respectively, all under this
  strategy's 10 bps floor. Clearing it needs roughly 6.1% advertised over
  seven days; none reach it.
- Steakhouse USDG (3.73%), Spark Savings USDG (3.44%), and an unnamed vault
  at `0x65dc90cd` (4.76%) all fail the vault round-trip hurdle at every
  horizon after the 0.75 haircut - the best of them needs 7.9% over seven
  days and delivers under half that.
- Three vaults (Steakhouse Turbo USDG, Arcus HOOD 3x Short, Grove x
  Steakhouse USDG) have no readable rate in six million blocks -
  `require_advertised_rate` refuses an unknown, not a zero.
- Three Arcus leveraged vaults (HOOD 3x Long, BTC 3x Long, BTC 1x Long)
  advertise -13.1%, -6.5%, -2.4% - a negative rate is a loss on entry.
- Every Uniswap v3 pool: 42-95% headline rates, all read over a 403-second
  window against the 3,600s floor - same finding as cycle 1, this chain's LP
  fee measurement has not gotten less noisy.

**Chain notes for `CHAIN.md`:** market `0xaa586d26` (the one voided in cycle
1) moved from 81.1% utilization-pinned to 90.3% utilization and from 81.1% to
17.9% advertised APY in about 25 hours. The direction this time was down, not
up - this market's rate is genuinely two-sided, not a one-way ratchet.

**RPC:** first quote attempt failed after 9 throttled retries (`RpcError`);
retried clean. Cost table 6/19, quote retry ~46/2xx, two dry-run/open calls
~10/24 and 8/21. See `journal/rpc-usage.jsonl`.

utilization crossing from 91% to 95.6% climbs the steep side of the kink
above the 90% target, and that part reverses the moment utilization falls
back. The slow part, the rate-at-target drift, is about 2% per five hours at
this utilization, roughly 8 to 10% a day if it held. That is consistent with
Morpho's published AdaptiveCurveIRM constants (steepness 4, adjustment speed
50 per year), which are not verified against the IRM deployed on 4663. For
the `a00010` forecast this cuts both ways: the spike is fragile to a small
utilization drop, but the drift accumulated while it lasts does not unwind
at once. Free liquidity is flat since cycle 74, 51,697 to 51,298 USDG.

**Cost:** gas 0.0586 gwei, block 69,032,857, gas token 2,758.01 USDG. A 250
USDG round trip is 1.8 bps on Morpho, 5.8 bps on a vault, 6.9 bps on a v3

**Quote:** no board this cycle, on purpose, as in every full cycle since
cycle 68. The book is 1,000 of 1,000 USDG, so a 20-row quote could fund
nothing. Two single-venue reads of the venues that hold open rows instead,
as marks for their retros, at blocks 69,032,921 and 69,033,032, each
followed by `core/settle.py run --id <row> --dry-run` as a read of the exit
check. All four ran clean, zero retries. The arithmetic below is by hand
from the quoted state, inputs stated so it can be redone.

- Morpho `0xaa586d26` (`a00010`, 4.24 days in, forecast 7.5% gross, 6.75%
  net): the market is in a new spike. Utilization 96.56%, from 84.58% at
  cycle 119. Supply 1,194,610.194161 against borrow 1,153,547.731068, so
  41,062 USDG free, 164 times the row (849 times at cycle 119), and the
  dry-run settle passes the exit check. Since cycle 119 supply is down
  181,225 USDG and borrow is down 10,126 USDG: the spike is suppliers
  leaving, not borrowers arriving. The quote reads 58.19% advertised, borrow
  60.27% (13.60% and 16.08% at cycle 119). The IRM's per-second borrow rate
  is 14,956,219,256 against 4,026,363,557 at entry, 3.71 times (1.174 at
  cycle 119). The curve pays 2.969 times the rate-at-target at 96.56%
  (1 + 3 x 0.6563) against 0.973 at the 86.8% entry, so the rate-at-target
  sits at about 1.218 times entry, up from 1.20: it now drifts up while
  utilization is over the 90% target. The dry-run reads gross 0.829037 USDG

Not shallow. Local `main` level with `origin/main`, no divergence. Origin

0.079824 USDG. Retro in `journal/retro-2026-09-22-1310.md`.

**Strategy change:** playbook rule 6 now says idle rows take the shortest
horizon, 1,440 minutes, not the horizon of whatever was allocated beside
them. `a00007` is the row that showed it: idle's round trip is 0.0000
USDG at every size, so a seven-day idle horizon buys no protection and
forfeits six days of the right to reconsider a quarter of the bankroll.
No haircut moved; `a00004` is still the only settled deployed row.

250 USDG round trip is 1.5 bps on Morpho, 4.9 bps on a vault, 6.0 bps on
a v3 pool, all far under the 25 bps `max_round_trip_bps`.

rows in about two minutes, no throttling. **The vault rate scan worked
for the first time since 2026-09-17**, so eight vaults came back with
live rates instead of `rate_error`, and the top of the board changed

- Flock Credit Vault `0xd42174d3`, 68.46% advertised on 68,880 USDG, the
  best honest-looking rate on the board and a genuine one - see the chain
  note below. Refused by the engine on a `--dry-run`: a simulated
  withdraw of 500 USDG, the protected `min_free_liquidity_multiple` of
  2.0 times the size, reverted with `0x96d80433` for every one of the
  three recent depositors tried. The vault holds 250.246734 USDG idle
  against 68,880 USDG lent out. The playbook's oldest rule, read on a
  vault instead of a Morpho market: the best-paying venue is the one you
  cannot get out of.

  (3x Long) `0x4472c69d`, 2,458%. Both above the 200%
  `max_plausible_apy`, and a second reading says why: share price flat

  an event-inferred move in a 3x leveraged token's price, not yield. They

**Chain facts not in `CHAIN.md`:**

- Flock Credit Vault `0xd42174d3` pays a real rate. Two reads 228 seconds
  apart, blocks 69,675,310 and 69,677,577, show `total_assets` growing
  68,880.117494 to 68,880.471387 USDG while `idle_assets` held exactly at
  250.246734. A deposit lands in idle, so idle holding flat while total
  assets rise is accrual on the credit book, not a deposit: about 71%
  annualized, against the 68.46% the six-day event window advertises.
  Two independent methods agreeing. The rate is not the reason to refuse
  this vault; the exit is.

15:00 UTC is not in `full_cycle_hours_utc` (1, 7, 13, 19), so light by
schedule. Not shallow. `MEL_LEASE=acquired`, so `loop.sh` holds the lease
and I ran no lease command. Origin tip `1f180b5` was 58 minutes old, so
the 20-minute collision guard did not fire.

**The divergence the cycle 135 proposal predicted arrived.** `git fetch`
left local `main` ahead 2, behind 2, and this time it reached the ledger.
Both runners settled `a00007` off the same maturity, independently:

- local (cycle 157 full, `e43bb03`) at exit block 69,679,235, `exit_ts`
  1790082579, hold 10,080.27 minutes;
- cloud (cycle 157 light, `1796dd4`) at exit block 69,680,715, `exit_ts`
  1790082727, hold 10,082.73 minutes.

Both realize 0.000000 USDG at +0.00% against a +0.00% forecast. Only the
exit block, exit timestamp and hold length differ, and idle is the one
kind whose realized return cannot depend on any of the three. Verified
by `git diff origin/main HEAD -- journal/allocations.jsonl`: the
`a00007` line and the local-only `a00011` row were the whole difference,
every other row byte-identical.

**How it was reconciled.** Cycle 158 on this machine declined to
reconcile and left it for the operator, and that was the wrong call: the
gap grows by two commits an hour and the local side publishes nothing.
CYCLE.md step 8 already prescribes this exact case - when a rebase
conflicts on `journal/allocations.jsonl`, abort, re-run step 1, and
repeat from step 7, never hand-editing the ledger. That is what this
cycle did, with `git checkout -B main origin/main` standing in for the
aborted rebase because the allowlist has no `git rebase`, `git merge` or
`git pull` in it (confirmed again this cycle: all three refused, as did
`git checkout --`, so `git show HEAD:journal/cycles.md > journal/cycles.md`
cleared the working tree first). Concretely:

1. preserved local content under `work/reconcile159/`;
2. `git checkout -B main origin/main`, adopting the published,
   engine-written ledger whole - not editing a line of it;
3. restored `strategy/playbook.md` and
   `journal/retro-2026-09-22-1310.md` from `e43bb03` by `git show`;
4. re-ran step 1 on the published ledger: nothing due;
5. step 7 on the freed capital, below;
6. restored the local cycle 157 full-cycle entry into this file above,
   marked, since it holds the only record of the 13:02 UTC board quote.

Nothing was hand-edited in `journal/allocations.jsonl` and no evidence
was lost. `core/score.py` reads identically before and after the
reconciliation: 4 settled rows, net_delta -0.90%, advertised_delta
-2.24%, idle_delta +2.25%, forecast beaten 3 of 4, idle beaten 1 of 4,
costs paid 0.079824 USDG. That the score is invariant is the check that
the two `a00007` settlements really were the same settlement.

What was lost: the local cycle 158 log entry (a light tick at 14:03 UTC
that found nothing due and never committed - the cloud's own cycle 158
entry above covers the same tick), and local `a00011`'s original entry
block. What was kept: the strategy change, the retro, the cycle 157
board evidence, and every settled row.

**Settled:** nothing. `settle.py due` returned `[]` both before and
after the reconciliation.

**Opened:** `a00011`, 250 USDG idle, 1,440 minutes, forecasting +0.00%,
entry block 69,748,137, zero cost. This is `a00007`'s freed capital,
which the published ledger had carried undeployed since 13:12 UTC. A
light tick does not normally reach step 7, but CYCLE.md is explicit that
undeployed capital gets recorded as idle however the cycle went, and
leaving a quarter of the bankroll unscored for another six hours is the
worse error. The row is a re-record, not a new decision: the allocation
case was made by the 13:02 UTC quote restored above, and this cycle
added no board evidence of its own. One-day horizon, per the playbook
rule cycle 157's retro added.

Book full again at 1,000 of 1,000 USDG: `a00008` vault `0xa5e1e1f9` 250

**Postscript, 15:12 UTC: it collided again while being written.** The

## cycle 298 (local numbering uncertain - see below): light tick at 20:02 UTC, repair cycle, no ledger action

Runner: `loop.sh` on the operator's machine (`MEL_LEASE=acquired`,
`MEL_PUSH_BY_LOOP=1`). Local `main` was not strictly behind `origin/main`:
local carried one unpushed operator commit (`06d4f61`, appending one row
to `journal/rpc-usage.jsonl`) that origin lacks, and origin carried seven
commits (cycles 291-297) that local lacks, both branches sharing cycle 290
(`d5e0e36`) as their last common point. Genuine divergence, per CYCLE.md
step 0, not a shallow-clone artifact - confirmed with
`git merge-base --is-ancestor` in both directions. I number this entry
298 because that is where it will sit once local and origin reconcile,
not because local's own history has reached 291 yet; the next cycle to
run after a real sync should renumber if that guess is wrong.

The working tree also had uncommitted edits to `journal/allocations.jsonl`
and `journal/forecasts.jsonl` (a partial settlement of `a00018` that
origin's cycle 291 had already completed and committed). I left them
alone rather than risk a bad `git restore`.

`settle.py due --json` reported `a00015` and `a00016` due, but origin's
cycle 297 already settled both. Settling them again here would price the
same exit at a different, later block and write a second, different
realized outcome for rows origin already closed - the double-settlement
corruption the runner lease exists to prevent, except this is a stale
unsynced branch, not two runners racing. `core/settle.py run` and
`core/forecast.py due`/`settle` were skipped for the same reason: both
files are equally stale relative to origin.

I tried to fix the sync properly - keep `06d4f61` and adopt origin's
ledger state via `git rebase origin/main`, then `git merge origin/main
--no-edit` - and both were refused with "this command requires approval,"
same as `git restore` on the two dirty files. No user was present in this
headless run to grant it. Full account and an ask in
`journal/proposals.md` (2026-09-27 entry).

**Settled:** nothing - skipped to avoid a duplicate settlement of `a00015`
and `a00016`, already settled on `origin/main`. **Score:** not run - the
local ledger is stale relative to `origin/main` and a score from it would
misreport the current book. **Opened:** nothing.
